metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are tracked as an uptime metric, because a degraded fabric wastes GPU-hours before it produces an outage.

The measurement covers two surfaces, the facility's internal fabric and its external transit, and it is continuous rather than sampled at failure. Its placement is the point. The other uptime metrics in this group are UPS battery health and generator runtime, which protect the power chain, and SLA uptime compliance, which is the contractual scoreboard. Network health sits alongside them because for AI workloads it fails the way power fails, not as a clean stop but as a slow tax on work already paid for.

Distributed training is why that tax is severe. A run spread across GPUs synchronizes constantly, so loss and latency on the fabric convert directly into idle compute. Wasted GPU-hours are the first visible symptom, and an outage is the later one. Watching the fabric is therefore a compute-efficiency control, not only a reliability control.

What this does not establish is any threshold. There is no target loss rate, no latency budget, no measurement interval, and no facility or operator named. It says what is watched, not what counts as acceptable, so it cannot be used to compare one site against another.
